Spun out of #64 (close): the grouped block-FP8 expert backend met #64's correctness, graph-safety, and performance acceptance, but the **resident-memory cost of the FNUZ conversion cache** caps how many layers can run the grouped path and is the next structural lever.

## Measured ceiling (Beverin MI300A, 128 GiB total)

After the real-checkpoint load ~74.2 GiB is resident; the 8-token probe (L3 converted + cached, L4–L11 conversion OOM-swallowed) pushed to 103.5 GiB with **4.3 GiB free**. - **(b) FNUZ conversion cache: ~9.7 GiB/layer permanent.** The fp8 e4m3FN originals *and* the FNUZ copies are both resident, so the conversion cache roughly doubles expert weight memory. This caps grouped layers at ~5/9 here.

## Context

GLM-5.3-Flash (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`) runs sglang's **DeepseekSparseAttn**
(DSA) layer. When `index_kpool > 1`, a `kpool-1` live tail of recent tokens is
appended to the fixed `index_topk` columns and held in a **persistent FP8
cache** (`torch.float8_e4m3fn`). The cache compress/write path is a *separate*
set of Triton kernels from the attention **forward** that #51 / PR #52
targeted (`sparse_mla_fwd_decode_partial` in `tilelang_kernel.py`):

- `kpool_fp8_index.py:1174` — `_kpool_assemble_softmax_rotate_write_cache_kernel` (prefill / short-context path)
- `kpool_fp8_index.py:992`  — `_kpool_decode_update_and_maybe_write_cache_kernel` (decode path; first arg `buf_fp8_ptr`)
- host wrappers `kpool_assemble_softmax_rotate_write_cache` (L1257),
  `kpool_decode_update_and_maybe_write_cache` (L761),
  `scatter_kpool_tail_updates` (L1323 → kernel L1361, which is index-only and not FP8).

This is the **SM80 / NVIDIA (A100)** counterpart to #51 (which was gfx942 /
MI300A). PR #52 landed native `vk_dsa_sparse_fwd` / `vk_hip_dsa_sparse_fwd`
with **bf16 storage + fp32 accumulation** and a `tail_dim == 0` runtime branch,
wired into the **Beverin (ROCm) overlay**. The upstream CUDA image that
Bristen uses does **not** get that wiring, so on A100 the `flashmla_sparse`
backend still calls its own raw-FP8 Triton kernels — and SM80 Triton cannot
even declare `*fp8e4nv` in a kernel signature, so they JIT-fail on the first
forward.

Cookbook recipe: [`cookbook/deployments/llm/bristen/glm-53-flash/`](https://github.com/opentela-ai/cookbook/tree/main/deployments/llm/bristen/glm-53-flash) (A100, SM80). The model already serves validated on one Clariden GH200 node (jobs 3213420 / 3219525, gen-probe PASS) — this issue is about enabling A100 as a serving target, and the kpool JIT is the blocker that prevents even a go/no-go.

## Empirical trail (Bristen, A100-80GB, jobs 82473 → 82822)

GLM-5.3-Flash ships in **FP8 e4m3** (~306 GB). A100 has no native FP8 tensor
cores, so the Bristen recipe applies a local patch that upcasts the FP8
MoE expert weights/activations to the compute dtype *before* the Triton GEMM
launch (because SM80 Triton cannot declare `*fp8e4nv` there either). That
patch gets the engine to boot but leaves the DSA kpool cache untouched.

Two configurations, two different blockers, neither serves:

| Config | DSA backend | Failure | Root cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 node, TP4 (job **82473**) | `tilelang` (SM80 overlay default) | **first MoE forward OOM** | A100-80GB HBM floor: ~2.4 GiB/GPU free after the 75.3 GB FP8 weights; the bf16 expert-weight upcast transient (~2.25 GiB/layer) cannot coexist with KV cache + mamba state |
| 2 nodes, PP2 (job **82822**) | `flashmla_sparse` | **Triton JIT compile, before MoE** | DSA kpool cache is hardcoded `torch.float8_e4m3fn` → `tl.float8e4nv`; SM80 cannot declare `*fp8e4nv` |

2-node PP2 was the attempt to escape the 1-node HBM floor (more memory/GPU).
It escapes the OOM — and trades it for a *more fundamental* blocker: the
kpool cache JIT fails **earlier**, on the first forward, before MoE is ever
reached. There is **no config-only escape**: `_compress_write` runs on every
forward, and no DSA backend yields a serving path on A100 (`tilelang` → HBM
floor at MoE; `flashmla_sparse` → kpool FP8 JIT; `fa3` → rejects GLM-5.3's
QK/V head dims on SM80).

## Root cause (observed, job 82822)

First forward, short-context path (`_forward_cuda_skip_logits`), post-PR-#52
(run `[2026-09-02T18:51:43] applying SM80 FP8 compute patches`, i.e. Sep 2 —
PR #52 merged Aug 30, so the kpool path is still raw FP8 Triton on the CUDA
image):

```
File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer_kpool.py", line 1464, in _forward_cuda_skip_logits
    self._compress_write(
File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer_kpool.py", line 573, in _compress_write
    return self._compress_write_extend(
File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer_kpool.py", line 408, in _compress_write_extend
    kpool_assemble_softmax_rotate_write_cache(
File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/kpool_fp8_index.py", line 1293, in kpool_assemble_softmax_rotate_write_cache
    _kpool_assemble_softmax_rotate_write_cache_kernel[(n_pools,)](
...
triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError: at 1:0:
def _kpool_assemble_softmax_rotate_write_cache_kernel(
^
ValueError("type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture. The supported fp8 dtypes are ('fp8e4b15', 'fp8e5')")
```

`_kpool_decode_update_and_maybe_write_cache_kernel` (L992, first arg
`buf_fp8_ptr`) is the decode counterpart and was not reached in 82822 (it
failed at the first-forward prefill kernel); it carries the same
`tl.float8e4nv` pattern and is expected to JIT-fail identically on SM80.

## The gap

Native **CPU oracle + SM80 CUDA** kernels for the two FP8 kpool-cache Triton
kernels above, mirroring PR #52's `dsa.{hpp,cpp,hip}` two-implementation
model and the `gemm_bf16` bf16-storage convention — **bf16 storage + fp32
accumulation, no `fp8e4nv` in any kernel signature** — plus the sglang
integration that wires them into the `flashmla_sparse` backend's
`_compress_write` / `_compress_write_extend` path on the upstream CUDA image.

Concretely, the equivalent of:
- `src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa_kpool.{hpp,cpp}` — `dsa_kpool_compress_write_cpu` (stable fp32 oracle), `dsa_kpool_compress_write` (bf16 storage, fp32 accum)
- C ABI `vk_dsa_kpool_compress_write` / `vk_hip_dsa_kpool_compress_write` in `src/c/vkernels/capi/`
- Python `dsa_kpool_compress_write` in `kernels.py` (+ `_core`/`_fallback`)
- Tests in `tests/kernels/attn/test_dsa_kpool.cpp` + a `meta/benchmarks/test_dsa_kpool_correct.hip`
- sglang wiring so the upstream CUDA image's `dsa/dsa_indexer_kpool.py::_compress_write*` calls the new kernel instead of `_kpool_assemble_softmax_rotate_write_cache_kernel` / `_kpool_decode_update_and_maybe_write_cache_kernel`

The decode counterpart (`kpool_decode_update_and_maybe_write_cache`) and the
prefill/short kernel (`kpool_assemble_softmax_rotate_write_cache`) are the
two that must drop `fp8e4nv`; `scatter_kpool_tail_updates` (L1361) is
index-only and not affected.

### Alternative (stopgap, lower-effort)

A source-level patch to `kpool_fp8_index.py` + `dsa_indexer_kpool.py` that
re-layouts the kpool cache to **bf16** on SM80 (allocate/store/read in bf16,
drop the `buf.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)` sites at L709/716/721/813/1289/1687
+ the `k_fp8` view sites in `dsa_indexer_kpool.py` L221/1007/1117/1319/1348).
This avoids the JIT without a new native kernel but runs slow bf16 Triton on
A100 and doubles the kpool cache footprint — likely fine for the kpool tail
(small relative to weights/KV) but not the durable solution PR #52's pattern
provides. Either approach removes the blocker; the native kernel is
preferred.

## Acceptance

- Host CI (`host` preset, no GPU): new `vkernels_test_dsa_kpool` passes, full ctest no new regressions.
- Real A100 / SM80 (Bristen): the first-forward JIT is gone — a short-context generation completes through `_compress_write` on the `flashmla_sparse` backend without `ValueError("type fp8e4nv ...")`.
- End-to-end: with 2-node PP2 (already wired in the sbatch, escapes the 1-node HBM floor from 82473), the mandatory `gen_correctness.py` probe reaches `verdict=PASS pass=5/6 crisp=3/3` — parity with the validated Clariden runs (jobs 3213420 / 3219525).

## Scope / non-goals

- The **1-node HBM floor** (82473) is not fixed here; it is escaped by running 2-node PP2 (already wired in the sbatch).
- The **non-kpool** DSA indexer (`dsa_indexer.py`, the `index_kpool == 1` path) has its own FP8 view sites (L1142/L1144/L1439/L1481). Out of scope here, but likely needs the same bf16 treatment if that path is exercised on SM80.
- End-to-end A100 serving is **not yet validated** even with this kernel — further FP8 paths may remain behind the kpool one. This issue removes the kpool JIT so the run can progress and produce a concrete go/no-go.

## Context

Kimi-K3 on Beverin (MI300A / gfx942) currently runs **attention through
vLLM's `TRITON_MLA` backend** and **disables KDA entirely**
(`K3_DISABLE_KDA=1`). Both are on the critical path of every K3 forward
pass (61 attention layers + KDA layers), and both have validated vkernels
HIP alternatives (issue #21) that are not wired into vLLM:

- **MLA** — `vk_mla_fwd` (`src/c/vkernels/kernels/mla.{hpp,hip}`),
  validated on MI300A (`test_mla_correct.hip`, 6 cases incl. K3 shapes).
  vLLM selects `TRITON_MLA` because AITER MLA requires gfx950 (the
  `_use_k3_situ_aiter` path is patched to `False` in `sitecustomize.py`),
  and there is no VKERNELS MLA backend in vLLM's attention selector.
- **KDA** — `vk_kda_delta_rule_fwd` (`src/c/vkernels/kernels/kda.{hpp,hip}`),
  validated on MI300A (`test_kda_correct.hip`, 12 cases incl. K3 head
  shapes). The AITER / Triton chunked KDA kernels **GPU-fault on gfx942**
  (job 586165), so K3 serving sets `K3_DISABLE_KDA=1`, which silently drops
  the delta-rule attention layer and degrades output quality.

The `VKERNELS_MXFP4_BF16` MoE backend (issue #20, cookbook commit
`1a0d792`) already demonstrated the integration pattern: a vLLM `Experts`
subclass (`VkernelFusedExperts` in `vkernels_experts.py`) calls the vkernels
C ABI (`libvkernels_hip.so`) via `ctypes`, injected at runtime through
`sitecustomize.py`. The same pattern can replace `TRITON_MLA` and re-enable
KDA, but neither is wired in today.

## The gap

### MLA

vLLM's attention layer calls `get_attention_cls()`, which dispatches to
`TRITON_MLA` for K3 on gfx942 (AITER MLA is gated on gfx950). A `VkernelMLA`
attention backend — registered in `sitecustomize.py` and selected ahead of
`TRITON_MLA` on gfx942 (via `torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).gcnArchName`,
the same guard `VkernelFusedExperts._supports_current_device` uses) — would
call `vk_mla_fwd` through the C ABI. The C ABI signature (already added
locally in the cookbook, pending a separate upstream issue) is:

```c
vk_mla_fwd(int B, int H, int S_q, int S_kv, int q_start, int kv_start,
           int kv_lora_rank, int qk_rope_head_dim, float scale,
           const float* q, const float* k_c, const float* k_pe,
           const float* v_c, float* out)
```

vLLM's MLA implementation already prepares `q`, `k_c`, `k_pe`, `v_c` in the
expected layout (compressed latent + decoupled RoPE); the shim needs to
extract the per-layer `q_start`/`kv_start` and `scale` from the vLLM
attention metadata and marshal the tensor `data_ptr()`s.

### KDA

KDA is disabled via `K3_DISABLE_KDA=1` because the AITER / Triton
`kda_delta_rule_fwd` kernels fault on gfx942. The vkernels
`vk_kda_delta_rule_fwd` kernel is validated and correct on gfx942
(`test_kda_correct.hip`, 12 cases incl. a chunked-vs-naive cross-check at
K3 head shapes). A `VkernelKDA` backend — or simply patching the vLLM KDA
selector to call `vk_kda_delta_rule_fwd` on gfx942 — would re-enable the
layer without the fault, **improving output quality** (the delta-rule
attention is currently silently dropped) and potentially improving latency
(a native gfx942 kernel vs the disabled path's fallback).

The C ABI signature (already added locally in the cookbook):

```c
vk_kda_delta_rule_fwd(const float* q, const float* k, const float* v,
                      const float* g, const float* beta, float* out,
                      int B, int H, int S, int D, int chunk_size)
```

1. **`VkernelMLA` attention backend** — a vLLM attention class (registered

## Context

Kimi-K3 serving on Beverin (MI300A / gfx942) via the `VKERNELS_MXFP4_BF16`
vLLM backend (issue #20, `VkernelFusedExperts` calling `vk_fused_moe_mxfp4`
through the C ABI) is **correct** — 6/6 factual probes pass with both real
(job 597880) and dummy (jobs 597846, 598005) weights — but measures
**0.49–0.83× the throughput of the patched AITER FlyDSL kernel** at matched
(concurrency, output-length) points:

| Concurrency | out_tok | VKERNELS (tok/s) | AITER FlyDSL (tok/s) | VKERNELS / AITER |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 1   | 256 | 3.6    | 7.32*   | **0.49×** |
| 8   | 256 | 27.0   | 48.91   | 0.55× |
| 32  | 256 | 83.8   | 134.85  | 0.62× |
| 64  | 256 | 147.7  | 178.09  | 0.83× |
| 256 | 128 | 172.3  | ~415†   | ~0.42× |

\* AITER single-request measured at out=128 (no out=256 point in the sweep);
both are single-request so the per-token time is directly comparable
(VKERNELS 0.277 s/tok vs AITER 0.137 s/tok).
† AITER peak at C=256 out=512 (dummy-weight table in the cookbook
`BENCHMARK.md`); different output length, indicative of the scaling ceiling.

The gap is **largest at low concurrency** (0.49× at C=1) and **narrows at
high concurrency** (0.83× at C=64), indicating the kernel is
**latency-bound at low M** and the AITER kernel amortizes per-kernel
overhead better through its CK 2-stage pipeline.

Topology: TP=8 PP=3 across 6 MI300A nodes. Each MoE layer invokes
`vk_fused_moe_mxfp4` once per forward pass; K3 has 61 MoE layers. The
VKERNELS backend replaced the AITER FlyDSL kernel
(`module_moe_ck2stages_b16_fp4x2_preshuffle_off_b16_silu_per_1x32_mulWeightStage2`),
which exceeded the 64 KB LDS limit on gfx942 (jobs 583297–583962) and
required fragile text patches (`k3_patch.py` markers `GFX942_SW_LDS_FILL` /
`GFX942_K16_SPLIT` / `GFX942_SW_CVT` / `GFX942_ASYNC_OFF`).

Reproduce: `deployments/llm/beverin/kimi-k3-vllm/` in opentela-ai/cookbook
(jobs 597987, 598005; the `BENCH=1` sweep in
`serve_kimi_k3_otela_beverin.sbatch` + `benchmark.py`).

## The gap

Five specific AITER FlyDSL optimizations are absent from
`src/c/vkernels/kernels/moe_fused.hip`, each with a measured or inferred
impact. The AITER kernel name encodes its design:
`module_moe_ck2stages_b16_fp4x2_preshuffle_off_b16_silu_per_1x32_mulWeightStage2`
→ CK 2-stage, bf16, 2 fp4/byte, preshuffle off, SwiGLU, 1×32 micro-tile,
routing weight fused into stage 2.

### 1. Per-call `hipMalloc`/`hipFree` for `sorted_w` (host launcher)

`hip::fused_moe_mxfp4` (moe_fused.hip, host launcher) allocates and frees
`EM * sizeof(float)` for the routing-weight gather on **every call**:

```cpp
float* sorted_w = nullptr;
(void)hipMalloc(&sorted_w, EM * sizeof(float));
// ... gather_weights_kernel ...
(void)hipFree(sorted_w);
```

With 61 MoE layers × many forward passes per request, this is 122 allocator
round-trips per generated token. The xkernels Triton kernel reuses a
persistent buffer; the AITER CK kernel allocates its workspace once at
module load. `vkernels_experts.py` already allocates a `workspace13` tensor
that could host `sorted_w` too.

### 2. `atomicAdd` scatter in the down epilogue

`down_combine_kernel` (moe_fused.hip) writes each (token, col) contribution
with `atomicAdd(&out[token * hidden + oc], v)`. When `top_k > 1` (K3 uses
`top_k = 16`), multiple experts contribute to the same output element,
causing atomic contention. The AITER `mulWeightStage2` variant fuses the
routing-weight multiply and the combine into the GEMM epilogue using a
**segmented reduction** (no atomics): the sorted layout groups all `top_k`
contributions to the same token contiguously, so a warp-level segmented
reduce across the `top_k` rows for each (token, col) — possible because
`sorted_ids` groups by expert and the combine iterates in sorted order —
would avoid the atomics entirely.

### 3. No pipeline overlap between dequant and MFMA

The decode K-loop is fully serial:

```
load_a_tile → dequant_b_gate → dequant_b_up → __syncthreads → mfma → __syncthreads
```

Each K=64 tile stalls on the dequant before the MFMA can begin. The
`docs/kernels/moe_fused.md` "Current limitations / future work" notes that
**LDS double-buffering was tried and reverted** (it doubled LDS 6→12 KB,
halving occupancy, slowing decode ~50%), so the lever is **not** deeper
LDS pipelining. However, the AITER CK kernel achieves overlap without
doubling LDS through **wavefront specialization** (a producer wavefront
fills LDS while a consumer wavefront issues MFMA on the previous tile) —
also noted as future work in moe_fused.md ("once occupancy saturates").
With the current 64-thread / 1-wavefront block there is no room for
specialization, but the prefill path (256 threads, 4 wavefronts) could
experiment with a 2-wavefront producer/consumer split reusing the single
`sB` buffer.

### 4. Strided global reads in weight dequant

`dequant_b_16cols` reads `packed[n * stride_packed + kp_off + kp]` — a
strided access (stride = `hidden/2` for w13, `ispp/2` for w2). Each thread
reads `kBytesPerThread = 8` bytes in non-contiguous positions. AITER
supports a **preshuffle** weight format (the `_preshuffle_off` suffix
indicates it is available but disabled for this variant) that rearranges
packed fp4 weights once at load time for coalesced global reads during the
kernel. Since the 84 GiB/GPU MXFP4 weight buffer cannot be duplicated, a
**K-major** packing (currently N-major: `[E, N, K/2]`) or a partial
per-expert preshuffle on demand could improve read coalescing without
doubling memory.

### 5. Decode tile is fixed at BM=16, BN=64, 64 threads

The decode path uses the minimum MFMA tile (BM=16) with a single wavefront
(64 threads) per block. The moe_fused.md analysis shows the kernel is
**occupancy-bound** (prefill BN 128→64 lifted occupancy 2→3 blocks/CU,
~1.5× faster). A `__launch_bounds__` directive to cap VGPRs below 40, or a
BM=32 decode tile (2 wavefronts, more B-tile reuse per loaded A row), could
reach 4+ blocks/CU. The current 4-z-block N-split (`blockIdx.z ∈ {0,1,2,3}`,
each 16 columns) is a workaround for the >64-thread crash on gfx90a and may
not be optimal for gfx942 (228 CU, 4× the wavefronts of gfx90a).

## Proposed scope

1. **Persistent scratch buffer** for `sorted_w` (and `act_scratch` if the
   caller can provide it) — eliminate per-call `hipMalloc`/`hipFree`.
   Caller-provided scratch is the cleanest API; `vkernels_experts.py`
   already allocates `workspace13` which could be reused for `sorted_w`.

2. **Warp-level segmented combine** for the down epilogue — replace
   `atomicAdd` with a sorted-layout reduction. Validate against the CPU
   oracle (`fused_moe_mxfp4_cpu`) at `top_k = 1, 4, 16`.

3. **Occupancy-first tile exploration** for decode — `__launch_bounds__(64, 4)`
   or a BM=32 / 2-wavefront decode variant. Benchmark at M=1, 8, 32 against
   the current BM=16 kernel (the `moe_fused_bench` already measures these
   points).

4. **Preshuffle / K-major weight layout** study — measure the global-read
   coalescing improvement from a K-major packed layout `[E, K/2, N]` vs the
   current N-major `[E, N, K/2]`. If the improvement is >20%, add a one-time
   preshuffle pass (callable from `k3_patch.py` at weight-load time) and a
   `dequant_b_kmajor` variant.

5. **Wavefront-specialized producer/consumer** for prefill — once items 1–3
   are in, experiment with a 2-wavefront split (1 producer dequant + 1
   consumer MFMA) in the 256-thread prefill kernel, reusing the single
   `sB` buffer (producer writes while consumer reads the previous tile).

## Acceptance

- All five improvements are validated against the CPU oracle
  (`max_rel < 0.00001` decode, `< 0.02` prefill) at K3 shapes
  (E=256, hidden=7168, ispp=33792, top_k=16).
- `moe_fused_bench` on MI300A shows the single-request decode (M=1)
  latency improving by ≥1.5× toward the AITER baseline
  (current ~0.45 ms → target ≤0.30 ms).
- K3 serving throughput (jobs 597880 / 598005 methodology) reaches
  ≥0.75× the AITER FlyDSL baseline at C=1 (target ≥5.5 tok/s) and
  ≥0.90× at C=64 (target ≥160 tok/s), without regressing correctness
  (6/6 factual probes).
- No per-call `hipMalloc`/`hipFree` in the host launcher (verified by
  `rocprof` kernel/alloc count).

The CPU reference (`fused_moe_mxfp4_cpu`) is the golden oracle every item validates against. Its dominant cost is dequanting the routed experts' MXFP4 weights, so I optimized `dequant_weight_tile` (LUT nibble→f32bits decode + per-group ue8m0 scale hoisting) **without changing results** — the original per-byte loop is kept as `dequant_weight_tile_ref`, and `test_moe_fused` asserts they're bit-identical (`Fp4DequantLUTBitExact` over every byte×scale, `Fp4DequantLUTHoistVaryingScale`, `K3RoutingTopK16`; 14/14 pass).

### 2. GPU kernel validated against the oracle on MI300A (acceptance #1, partial)

At the K3 routing shape (E=256, h7168, i512, top_k=16, `--kmajor`), the GPU kernel matches the optimized oracle with `cpu-rel < 0.03` and `status = ok` for every M, reproduced twice:

| M | EM | evt µs | cpu-rel | status |
|---|---:|-------:|--------:|--------|
| 1 | 256 | 1108 | 0.00157 | ok |
| 2 | 512 | 1251 | 0.029 | ok |

Default harness (E=256, h4096, i512, k6, SwiGLU): M=1 = **398 µs** ≈ the ~0.45 ms baseline in the issue. Full log + table in `docs/performance/moe-fused/gfx942.md`.

### ⚠️ 3. New blocker: GPU memory-access fault at ispp ≥ 4096 / full K3 (worth a look)

Running the standalone `moe_fused_bench` at the **full K3 shape (ispp=33792)** — and at ispp≥4096 for E=256 — faults on the GPU:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-4 (Agent handle: ...) on address 0x...  Reason: Unknown.
```

This is **not** memory pressure (E=32, the per-GPU TP=8 shard, is only ~12 GB resident) and **not** the K-major path (item 4) — it faults identically with and without `--kmajor`. It's a deeper internal index/stride assumption at large ispp.

The reason this matters: the issue reports K3 serving **works** (6/6 factual probes, jobs 597880/598005) at ispp=33792 through the vLLM backend — so the same weights/shape run fine in serving but fault in this single-GPU bench. - **End-to-end serving throughput (criterion #3)** — not measured here; that's the cookbook `BENCH=1` sweep, unchanged.

### Key finding (KDA integration approach needs re-architecting)
On this image the AMD K3 model instantiates **`KimiGatedDeltaNetAttention`**
(`vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.gdn.kimi_gdn_linear_attn`, via
`models.kimi_k3.amd.linear` line ~471 for every `is_kda_layer` index) — **not**
`KimiK3DeltaAttention` (`vllm.models.kimi_k3.nvidia.kda`, NVIDIA-only). The
older file I'd inspected had `KimiK3DeltaAttention` at `vllm.models.kimi_k3.amd.kda`,
which is gone in this build.

`KimiGatedDeltaNetAttention._forward` is far more than the bare delta-rule: it
performs **conv1d** (`causal_conv1d_fn`/`_update`), the **A_log→g /
dt_bias / lower_bound gate transform**, **initial_state gather**,
the **spec-vs-non-spec split**, and **recurrent-state writeback**, then
dispatches the delta-rule itself to the leaf kernels
`chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` (prefill) and `fused_recurrent_kda`/
`fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode` (decode) in
`vllm.models.kimi_k3.amd.ops.third_party.kda` — **the faulting kernels on gfx942**.

**leaf kernels** (preserving the conv1d + gate + initial_state + spec + state
bookkeeping in `_forward`), not to patch the attention class `_forward` with a
from-scratch `vk_hip_kda_delta_rule_fwd` call (which would skip all of that and
be wrong). The shipped code now (a) patches the correct class and (b) RAISES
`NotImplementedError` on real metadata + refuses to fall back to `orig_forward`

work lands. **`VKERNELS_MLA=1`** (MLA half) is lower-risk — registration is
validated; a `--load-format dummy` serve (TP1, `VKERNELS_MLA_VALIDATE=0` until
the CPU oracle `libvkernels_c.so` is built/deployed) is the natural next step to
validate `forward_mqa` end-to-end.

## Journal

**What was done.** Validated the fused MoE (decode + prefill) and the four
primitives on MI300A (gfx942) after the gfx90a bring-up, and recorded the
results under `docs/performance/`. Prefill correctness passes at
`max_rel < 0.02`, decode at `max_rel < 0.00001`.

**Challenges.**
1. *Cross-node image loading.* SLURM jobs land on different MI300A nodes,
   none of which share the login node's podman storage. The working recipe
   is a fresh per-job `podman --root $PR/root --runroot $PR/run load` into
   `/tmp` (the default `/dev/shm` root carries a stale boot-ID after node
   reboots and fails with exit 125).
2. *Triton baseline unavailable.* xkernels' Triton backend SIGSEGVs under
   ROCm 6.2.4 + Triton 3.3.1 on both architectures, so the baseline is the
   torch loop (which gfx942 also accelerates ~1.3× over gfx90a).
3. *Occupancy was the real lever.* Narrowing the prefill BN 128→64 (24→16 KB
   LDS, 64→32 accumulator VGPRs) lifted occupancy 2→3 blocks/CU and won
   ~1.3–1.8× on gfx942, consistent with the ~1.5× measured cleanly on gfx90a.

**Future work.**
- Raise occupancy further: a BM=32 prefill tile (or `__launch_bounds__`
  nudging) could cut VGPRs below 64 and reach 4 blocks/CU; split gate/up to
  reduce live registers is another path.
- Wavefront-specialised producer/consumer dequant once occupancy saturates.
- Revisit the Triton baseline when ROCm 6.3 / a fixed Triton ships.

def e4m3fn_to_fnuz(w_fp8, scales):
    """e4m3fn -> e4m3fnuz with the payload-halving trick (one-time).

    gfx942's fp8 tensor cores and fp8->fp32 conversions are FNUZ-semantics
    (bias 4, max finite 240); checkpoint e4m3fn has bias 7 / max 448, so a
    VALUE-preserving cast overflows to NaN for payloads in (240, 448].
    Instead: halve every payload (EXACT for fp8 normals — one exponent
    decrement, mantissa untouched; subnormals round to the coarser fnuz
    subnormal grid) and DOUBLE the per-block scales, so payload x scale is
    unchanged. Returns (w_fnuz, scales_x2)."""
    import torch

    if w_fp8.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fnuz:
        return w_fp8, scales
    half = (w_fp8.to(torch.float32) * 0.5).to(torch.float8_e4m3fnuz)
    return half, scales * 2.0

TITLE: feat(python): capture-safe vLLM MoE integration (issue #41, #42)
BODY: ## What

Promotes the validated, capture-safe vkernels HIP MoE backend out of the cookbook (`VkernelFusedExperts`, currently duplicated across two cookbook copies) into a first-class **optional** integration module: `vkernels.vllm_experts`. This is the root-cause fix for the `Memory access fault` crashes that made the **breakable piecewise cudagraph path unusable on gfx942 with PP=3** (issue #42), and the place the issue #41, item 1 "caller owns and reuses scratch" contract is finally enforced by the library instead of reimplemented (and broken) by every caller.

`import vkernels` stays **numpy-only**; the new module is pulled in only on `from vkernels.vllm_experts import ...` (registered in `__init__._LazyIntegration`). On CI (no torch) the new file is importable for its numpy-only surface; the torch tests skip cleanly.

## Two layers

**`CaptureSafeScratch`** — the reusable, torch-only persistent-scratch manager. Each `(device, key)` buffer (`act_scratch`, `out`, `sorted_ids`, `expert_ids`) is sized **once** on the eager profile/warmup run (before any CUDA-graph capture) at the `MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS` high-water mark and sliced into forever after, so the storage address is replay-stable. **Growing while a capture session is active is refused** (the freed storage is referenced by the captured graph → `Memory access fault` on replay) — exactly the bug that crashed the per-call `torch.empty()` wrapper (16 faults in ~9 min, job 602311). Capture detection is injectable; `_vllm_capture_probe` also covers the `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture` eager-break window where `is_current_stream_capturing()` is False but a session is live.

**`VkernelFusedExperts`** — the vLLM `UnfusedOAITritonExperts` subclass that drives `vk_hip_fused_moe_mxfp4` (PR #44) via ctypes on gfx942 / Kimi-K3, launches on PyTorch's *current* stream (no per-launch device sync → each MoE layer is no longer a cross-stream TP barrier), and backs all C-ABI scratch with `CaptureSafeScratch`. Built lazily (imports vLLM on first use).

Also: `moe_align_block_size_with_map` (the `expert_map`-aware, TP-sharded CPU helper, parity-checked against `vkernels.kernels.moe_align_block_size`) and `find_libvkernels_hip` (`VKERNELS_LIB` / `$K3` / `$VKERNELS_DIR` / system resolution).

## Validation (cookbook job 602516, MI300A / TP8 PP3 / 6 nodes)

| Metric | ENFORCE_EAGER baseline (602367) | breakable + fix (602516) | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Faults under capture | — (no capture) | **0 over 58 min** (was 16 in ~9 min) | |
| C=1 single-stream | 3.7 tok/s | **6.0 tok/s** | **1.62×** |
| C=8 aggregate | 22.7 tok/s | **38.6 tok/s** | **1.70×** |
| C=1 latency p50 | 68.7 s | **42.9 s** | **1.60× lower** |

C=32/C=64 timed out on **both** jobs — a harness artifact (`max_num_seqs=8` serializes 32 reqs into 4 batches × ~53 s > the 180 s per-req timeout), not a path defect. Full writeup in the cookbook `BENCHMARK.md` (commit e14775f).

## Tests

`tests/python/test_vllm_experts.py` — 21 tests:
- `CaptureSafeScratch` persistent reuse + capture-refusal + within-capacity-slice (torch, skipped without torch)
- `moe_align_block_size_with_map` parity vs the canonical `kernels.moe_align_block_size` + skip-map behavior (numpy, runs on CI)
- `find_libvkernels_hip` env resolution (numpy, runs on CI)
- `VkernelFusedExperts` lazy-build + `import vkernels` does not pull vLLM (subprocess)

On this host (numpy 2.5, no torch): **12 passed, 9 skipped** (the skipped are the torch tests). Full suite: **188 passed**, 1 pre-existing failure (`test_discovery.py::test_kernel_names_and_order`, fails on `main` too — new C kernels `moe_gateup_preact`/`sum` added without updating the expected list; unrelated to this PR).

## Stacking note

This branch includes commit `1079694` (perf(moe): launch fused MXFP4 on the caller's stream, drop device sync) as a prerequisite — it adds the `stream` arg this module's ctypes call passes, and is local-only (no open PR). Kept here so the PR is self-contained/buildable; **happy to split it out as its own PR first** and rebase this on top if preferred.

## Files

- `src/python/vkernels/vllm_experts.py` (new) — the integration module
- `src/python/vkernels/__init__.py` — register `vllm_experts` in `_LazyIntegration`
- `tests/python/test_vllm_experts.py` (new)
- `docs/python-bindings.md`, `docs/kernels/moe_fused.md` — integration + caller-contract docs

perf(amd): MoE reads topk_w directly, K-major weights, launch bounds (#41, items 2-4)

The down-combine epilogue now reads topk_w[flat] directly, where
flat = sorted_ids[...] is already guarded by flat < M*top_k.  This
removes the per-forward gather_weights_kernel and the sorted_w[EM]
scratch buffer the launcher allocated and populated -- one fewer
kernel launch and one fewer per-call device buffer per forward, on
top of item 1's caller-owned act_scratch.

K-major gate/up weight packing [E,2,hidden/2,ispp] (N contiguous)
behind a `kmajor` launcher flag + matching dequant_b_16cols_kmajor
and a bench `--kmajor` repack (item 4).  The 16 dequant columns each
decode block owns then read one coalesced 16-byte cache line per
K-step instead of 16 scattered lines.  Measured batched steady-state
at the harness shapes (E=256, hidden=4096, ispp=512, gfx942):
K-major is slower at M=1-4 (479 vs 395 us), even at M=8, faster at
M>=16 (1688 vs 2034 us at M=16); crossover ~M=8.  Default stays
N-major -- K-major is a throughput optimization, not a decode-latency
one.

Add __launch_bounds__ to all four MoE kernels (item 3): decode gateup
(64,10) / down (64,16), prefill gateup+down (256,4).  On gfx942 the
prefill kernels are LDS-limited at 4 blocks/CU and the decode kernels
are grid-limited (192 blocks for 228 CUs at M=1), so this documents
intent rather than raising occupancy.

"""Gather checkpoint E4M3FN experts and block-dequantize to BF16/FP16.

Decode the stored bytes explicitly: gfx942's native E4M3FNUZ conversion has
different zero/NaN encodings and exponent bias from checkpoint E4M3FN.
Only the output is allocated; FP32 products remain in kernel registers.

Adopted from floe's ``engine/runner/kernels/fp8_experts.py`` (vkernels owns
the kernel; floe imports it back through a thin adapter — the #64/#65
thin-adapter model extended to the whole GLM-5 Triton set).

Torch and Triton load lazily. Inference-only, no autograd backward.
"""

from functools import lru_cache


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def _kernel():
    global tl
    import triton
    import triton.language as tl

    @triton.jit
    def _gather_dequant(
        W, S, IDX, Y, O: tl.constexpr, I: tl.constexpr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr
    ):
        selected = tl.program_id(0)
        offset = tl.program_id(1) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
        mask = offset < O * I
        expert = tl.load(IDX + selected).to(tl.int64)
        raw = tl.load(W + expert * (O * I) + offset, mask, 0).to(tl.int32)
        exponent = (raw >> 3) & 15
        mantissa = raw & 7
        # Normal E4M3FN numbers have bias 7; all exponent-15 values except
        # mantissa 7 are finite. Bit construction is exact in FP32.
        bits = ((exponent + 120) << 23) | (mantissa << 20)
        value = tl.where(
            exponent == 0,
            mantissa.to(tl.float32) * 0.001953125,
            bits.to(tl.float32, bitcast=True),
        )
        value = tl.where((raw & 127) == 127, float("nan"), value)
        # Preserve -0 explicitly: arithmetic negation can be folded to 0-x,
        # which produces +0 for a zero input on the HIP compilation path.
        value = (value.to(tl.int32, bitcast=True) | ((raw & 128) << 24)).to(
            tl.float32, bitcast=True
        )
        scale_offset = (expert * (O // 128) + offset // I // 128) * (I // 128)
        scale_offset += (offset % I) // 128
        scale = tl.load(S + scale_offset, mask, 0)
        tl.store(Y + selected.to(tl.int64) * (O * I) + offset, value * scale, mask)

    return _gather_dequant

    tile map, two grouped launches, one swiglu + per-row quantize — no

order can differ from rocBLAS.

Adopted from floe's ``engine/runner/kernels/glm5_fp8_gemv.py`` (the
decode-validated implementation; measured ~1.0 TB/s effective at the GLM
top-8 dispatch on MI300A — faster than a per-matrix native kernel there).
floe imports this back through a thin adapter so vkernels owns the kernel
(#65's thin-adapter model) while floe keeps a local fallback.

autograd backward. Graph capture: warm up eagerly per shape first (the

    one program per (token, expert-slot) pair — so only the wrapper guard
    needs lifting; parity at the raised T is checked by the caller's job."""

def e4m3fn_to_fnuz(w_fp8, scales):
    """e4m3fn -> e4m3fnuz with the payload-halving trick (one-time).

    gfx942's fp8 tensor cores and fp8->fp32 conversions are FNUZ-semantics
    (bias 4, max finite 240); checkpoint e4m3fn has bias 7 / max 448, so a
    VALUE-preserving cast overflows to NaN for payloads in (240, 448].
    Instead: halve every payload (EXACT for fp8 normals — one exponent
    decrement, mantissa untouched; subnormals round to the coarser fnuz
    subnormal grid) and DOUBLE the per-block scales, so payload x scale is
    unchanged. Returns (w_fnuz, scales_x2)."""
    import torch

    if w_fp8.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fnuz:
        return w_fp8, scales
    half = (w_fp8.to(torch.float32) * 0.5).to(torch.float8_e4m3fnuz)
    return half, scales * 2.0


@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
def _fnuz_byte_lut(device):
    """256-entry e4m3fn -> e4m3fnuz byte map on ``device``.

    The halving conversion is a PURE per-byte function — halving an fp8
    value is an exact exponent decrement, subnormals land exactly on the
    fnuz subnormal grid, NaN (0x7f) maps to fnuz NaN (0x80) and fn -0
    (0x80) maps to fnuz +0 (0x00); verified exhaustive over all 256 bytes
    against this module's fp32-roundtrip reference. So the conversion needs
    no fp32 materialization of the weight stack at all: it is a byte gather
    through this table."""
    import torch

    raw = torch.arange(256, dtype=torch.uint8)
    fn = raw.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    fz = (fn.to(torch.float32) * 0.5).to(torch.float8_e4m3fnuz)
    return fz.view(torch.uint8).to(device, non_blocking=True)


def e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(w_fp8, scales, chunk_bytes=1 << 26):
    """In-place e4m3fn -> e4m3fnuz (issue #71): rewrite ``w_fp8``'s bytes to
    the halved-payload fnuz encoding and double ``scales`` in place, so the
    converted stack SHARES the checkpoint's storage.

    This removes both resident-memory costs of the copy-based conversion
    (``e4m3fn_to_fnuz``): the fnuz copy is no longer a second ~1 B/element

def e4m3fn_to_fnuz(w_fp8, scales):
    """e4m3fn -> e4m3fnuz with the payload-halving trick (one-time).

    gfx942's fp8 tensor cores and fp8->fp32 conversions are FNUZ-semantics

    VALUE-preserving cast overflows to NaN for payloads in (240, 448].

    unchanged. Returns (w_fnuz, scales_x2)."""

    if w_fp8.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fnuz:
        return w_fp8, scales
    half = (w_fp8.to(torch.float32) * 0.5).to(torch.float8_e4m3fnuz)
    return half, scales * 2.0

"""e4m3fn -> e4m3fnuz IN-PLACE conversion (issue #71).

The grouped native-fp8 path's copy-based conversion cache doubled
expert-weight residency (~9.7 GiB/layer permanent) and its ~19 GiB fp32
transient OOM-swallowed conversions under a fixed HBM floor. The halving
map is a pure per-byte function, so ``e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace`` rewrites the
checkpoint bytes in place through a 256-entry LUT: the converted stack
shares the checkpoint's storage (no second resident copy) and no fp32
materialization (peak extra memory is chunk-sized). The fnuz-storage decode
variants (``expert_gemv`` / ``gather_dequant`` with ``storage="e4m3fnuz"``)
consume it with bit-identical values.
"""

import pytest


@pytest.fixture
def torch():
    return pytest.importorskip("torch")


def _byte_stack(torch, e=4, o=256, i=256, seed=11):
    """Full-range byte pattern: subnormals, both NaN encodings, -0, maxima."""
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    weights = torch.randint(
        0, 256, (e, o, i), dtype=torch.uint8, generator=g
    ).view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    scales = torch.rand((e, o // 128, i // 128), generator=g) * 0.1 + 0.01
    return weights, scales


def _value_stack(torch, e=4, o=256, i=256, seed=5):
    """Realistic NaN-free weights for output-bit-exactness comparisons."""
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    weights = (
        torch.randn((e, o, i), generator=g).clamp(-4, 4).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    )
    scales = torch.rand((e, o // 128, i // 128), generator=g) * 0.1 + 0.01
    return weights, scales


def test_lut_matches_reference_exhaustive(torch):
    from vkernels.torch_ops.glm_fp8_blockwise_gemm import _fnuz_byte_lut

    lut = _fnuz_byte_lut(torch.device("cpu"))
    raw = torch.arange(256, dtype=torch.uint8)
    fn = raw.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    expected = (fn.to(torch.float32) * 0.5).to(torch.float8_e4m3fnuz).view(torch.uint8)
    assert torch.equal(lut, expected)


def test_halving_is_value_exact(torch):
    """fnuz_decode(LUT[b]) * 2 == fn_decode(b) for every finite byte and NaN
    maps to NaN — consumers multiplying by the DOUBLED scales decode
    bit-identical values to the e4m3fn path."""
    from vkernels.torch_ops.glm_fp8_blockwise_gemm import _fnuz_byte_lut

    lut = _fnuz_byte_lut(torch.device("cpu"))
    raw = torch.arange(256, dtype=torch.uint8)
    fn_val = raw.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).to(torch.float32)
    fz_val = lut.view(torch.float8_e4m3fnuz).to(torch.float32)
    finite = torch.isfinite(fn_val)
    assert finite.sum() == 254  # only 0x7f/0xff are fn NaN
    assert torch.equal(fz_val[finite] * 2, fn_val[finite])
    assert torch.isnan(fz_val[raw == 0x7F]).all()
    assert fz_val[raw == 0x80] == 0.0  # fn -0 -> fnuz +0 (no -0 in fnuz)


def test_inplace_matches_reference_and_shares_storage(torch):
    from vkernels.torch_ops.glm_fp8_blockwise_gemm import (
        e4m3fn_to_fnuz,
        e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace,
    )

    weights, scales = _byte_stack(torch)
    ref_w, ref_s = e4m3fn_to_fnuz(weights.clone(), scales.clone())
    ptr = weights.data_ptr()
    w_fnuz, s2 = e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(weights, scales)
    assert w_fnuz.data_ptr() == ptr  # same storage — nothing extra resident
    assert w_fnuz.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fnuz
    assert s2 is scales  # doubled in place
    assert torch.equal(w_fnuz.view(torch.uint8), ref_w.view(torch.uint8))
    assert torch.equal(s2, ref_s)


def test_chunked_conversion_matches_single_shot(torch):
    from vkernels.torch_ops.glm_fp8_blockwise_gemm import e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace

    weights, scales = _byte_stack(torch, seed=3)
    w1, s1 = e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(weights.clone(), scales.clone())
    w2, s2 = e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(
        weights.clone(), scales.clone(), chunk_bytes=997
    )
    assert torch.equal(w1.view(torch.uint8), w2.view(torch.uint8))
    assert torch.equal(s1, s2)


def test_guards(torch):
    from vkernels.torch_ops.glm_fp8_blockwise_gemm import e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace

    weights, scales = _byte_stack(torch, e=2)
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="already e4m3fnuz"):
        e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(weights.view(torch.float8_e4m3fnuz), scales)
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="e4m3fn"):
        e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(weights.to(torch.float32), scales)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="contiguous"):
        e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(weights.transpose(0, 1), scales)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="storage"):
        e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(weights, scales, chunk_bytes=0) is None  # noqa: B015


def test_device_guard(torch):
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        pytest.skip("requires two devices")
    from vkernels.torch_ops.glm_fp8_blockwise_gemm import e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace

    weights, scales = _byte_stack(torch, e=2)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="device"):
        e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(weights.to("cuda"), scales)


def test_gpu_inplace_matches_cpu_reference(torch):
    """The production path: the LUT gather runs on-device."""
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        pytest.skip("requires GPU")
    from vkernels.torch_ops.glm_fp8_blockwise_gemm import (
        e4m3fn_to_fnuz,
        e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace,
    )

    weights, scales = _byte_stack(torch)
    ref_w, ref_s = e4m3fn_to_fnuz(weights.clone(), scales.clone())
    gpu_w, gpu_s = weights.to("cuda"), scales.to("cuda")
    w_fnuz, s2 = e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(gpu_w, gpu_s, chunk_bytes=1 << 20)
    assert w_fnuz.data_ptr() == gpu_w.data_ptr()
    assert torch.equal(w_fnuz.view(torch.uint8).cpu(), ref_w.view(torch.uint8))
    assert torch.equal(s2.cpu(), ref_s)


def test_expert_gemv_fnuz_storage_bit_exact(torch):
    """fnuz-storage GEMV on the in-place converted stack must decode the
    SAME values as the e4m3fn path on the original stack (halving is exact,
    scales are doubled) — outputs bit-identical on every backend."""
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        pytest.skip("requires GPU")
    pytest.importorskip("triton")
    from vkernels.torch_ops.glm_expert_gemv import expert_gemv
    from vkernels.torch_ops.glm_fp8_blockwise_gemm import e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace

    for device in ("cuda",):
        weights, scales = _value_stack(torch)
        x = torch.randn(2, 256, dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(1))
        indices = torch.rand((2, 4), generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(2)).topk(
            4, dim=-1
        ).indices.to(torch.int64)
        expected = expert_gemv(
            x.to(device), weights.to(device), scales.to(device), indices.to(device)
        )
        w_nz, s2 = e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(weights, scales)
        actual = expert_gemv(
            x.to(device),
            w_nz.to(device),
            s2.to(device),
            indices.to(device),
            storage="e4m3fnuz",
        )
        assert torch.equal(actual, expected)


def test_gather_dequant_fnuz_storage_bit_exact(torch):
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        pytest.skip("requires GPU")
    pytest.importorskip("triton")
    from vkernels.torch_ops.glm_expert_gather_dequant import gather_dequant
    from vkernels.torch_ops.glm_fp8_blockwise_gemm import e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace

    weights, scales = _value_stack(torch)
    indices = torch.rand((2, 4), generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(2)).topk(
        4, dim=-1
    ).indices.to(torch.int64)
    expected = gather_dequant(weights.cuda(), scales.cuda(), indices.cuda())
    w_nz, s2 = e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(weights, scales)
    actual = gather_dequant(
        w_nz.cuda(), s2.cuda(), indices.cuda(), storage="e4m3fnuz"
    )
    assert torch.equal(actual, expected)


def test_grouped_native_inplace_matches_reference(torch):
    """The grouped fp8 path consumes the in-place views exactly as it
    consumed the copy-based conversion — outputs bit-identical."""
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        pytest.skip("requires GPU")
    pytest.importorskip("triton")
    from vkernels.torch_ops.glm_fp8_blockwise_gemm import (
        e4m3fn_to_fnuz,
        e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace,
        glm_moe_grouped_gemm_native,
    )

    e, i, h, t, k = 4, 256, 256, 8, 2
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(9)
    gate_up = torch.randn((e, 2 * i, h), generator=g).clamp(-4, 4).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    down = torch.randn((e, h, i), generator=g).clamp(-4, 4).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    gu_sc = torch.rand((e, (2 * i) // 128, h // 128), generator=g) * 0.1 + 0.01
    dn_sc = torch.rand((e, h // 128, i // 128), generator=g) * 0.1 + 0.01
    x = torch.randn((t, h), generator=g).to(torch.bfloat16).cuda()
    topk_index = torch.rand((t, e), generator=g).topk(k, dim=-1).indices.to(torch.int64).cuda()
    topk_weights = torch.softmax(torch.rand((t, k), generator=g), dim=-1).cuda()

    ref = glm_moe_grouped_gemm_native(
        x, *e4m3fn_to_fnuz(gate_up.clone(), gu_sc.clone()),
        *e4m3fn_to_fnuz(down.clone(), dn_sc.clone()),
        topk_index, topk_weights,
    )
    gu_nz, gu_sc2 = e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(gate_up, gu_sc)
    dn_nz, dn_sc2 = e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(down, dn_sc)
    actual = glm_moe_grouped_gemm_native(
        x, gu_nz, gu_sc2, dn_nz, dn_sc2, topk_index, topk_weights
    )
    assert torch.equal(actual, ref)

grouped native-fp8 GEMM (glm_moe_grouped_gemm_native) at real shapes
(288 experts, top-8, checkpoint-layout weights).

Requires the one-time e4m3fn_to_fnuz weight conversion (done here); the
grouped path quantizes activations per row (w8a8 — the 4.4e-2 parity vs
the bf16 eager reference IS that quantization; quality A/B gates it).
"""
import os, time, torch
import vkernels.torch_ops.glm_fp8_blockwise_gemm as G

torch.manual_seed(731)
print("device:", torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))
E, H, I = 288, 4096, 2048
TOPK = 8

raw_gu = torch.randint(0, 256, (E, 2 * I, H), device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8)
raw_gu.masked_fill_((raw_gu & 127) == 127, 0)
gu8 = raw_gu.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
gu_sc = (0.0005 + torch.rand((E, 2 * I // 128, H // 128), device="cuda") * 0.002)
raw_dn = torch.randint(0, 256, (E, H, I), device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8)
raw_dn.masked_fill_((raw_dn & 127) == 127, 0)
dn8 = raw_dn.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
dn_sc = (0.0005 + torch.rand((E, H // 128, I // 128), device="cuda") * 0.002)

# one-time weight conversion (fnuz + doubled scales)
gu_nz, gu_sc2 = G.e4m3fn_to_fnuz(gu8, gu_sc)
dn_nz, dn_sc2 = G.e4m3fn_to_fnuz(dn8, dn_sc)

def moe_grouped_native(x, idx, wts):
    return G.glm_moe_grouped_gemm_native(
        x, gu_nz, gu_sc2, dn_nz, dn_sc2, idx, wts, swiglu_limit=7.0)

cfg = Glm53Config(n_routed_experts=E, hidden_size=H, moe_intermediate_size=I)
with torch.device("meta"):

experts_floe.gate_up_proj = torch.nn.Parameter(gu8, requires_grad=False)
experts_floe.gate_up_scale = gu_sc
experts_floe.down_proj = torch.nn.Parameter(dn8, requires_grad=False)
experts_floe.down_scale = dn_sc

def moe_batched(x, idx, wts):

    return experts_floe(x, idx, wts)

def moe_eager_ref(x, idx, wts):
    os.environ["GLM53_BATCHED_EXPERTS"] = "0"

content.text: GLM-5.3: 45 layers, E=288, H=4096, I=2048. Now I'll write the profiling harness locally, then rsync everything. The design: one script that runs under **either** stack (main snapshots = "old", my branch worktrees = "new"), with `PROF71_SECTIONS` gating — the same seed/inputs on both stacks lets me compare output hashes across runs:

input.content:
"""#71 on-cluster profile: in-place e4m3fn->e4m3fnuz conversion vs the
copy-based conversion cache, on a beverin MI300A (gfx942).

Runs under EITHER stack (selected via PYTHONPATH in the sbatch):
  - old: floe@main + vkernels@main  -> sections: floe (copy-cache evidence)
  - new: floe#17  + vkernels#72     -> sections: vk, floe
Same seeds/inputs on both -> printed output hashes must match across runs.

Sections (PROF71_SECTIONS, comma-separated):
  vk   - single-layer A/B memory table, conversion timing, bit-exact
         grouped parity old-vs-new, fnuz-storage decode parity
  cap  - K-layer sweep under the HBM floor: copy path OOMs partway,
         in-place path converts every layer and groups
  floe - floe Glm53Experts level: grouped engage, resident-delta table,
         in-place marker, decode-after-convert, output hashes
"""
import os, time, torch

SECTIONS = set(s.strip() for s in os.environ.get("PROF71_SECTIONS", "vk,cap,floe").split(",") if s.strip())
LABEL = os.environ.get("PROF71_LABEL", "?")

E, H, I, TOPK = 288, 4096, 2048, 8
SWIGLU = 7.0
HEADROOM_GIB = 22.0     # free-mem target when building the K-layer sweep
CHUNK = 64 * 2**20      # 64 MiB chunks for the in-place conversion

def log(*a):
    print("[71:%s]" % LABEL, *a, flush=True)

def gib(x):
    return x / 2**30

def make_stack(seed, e=E):
    """Checkpoint-layout fp8 expert stack (bench_fp8_grouped recipe)."""
    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
    raw_gu = torch.randint(0, 256, (e, 2 * I, H), device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8, generator=g)
    raw_gu.masked_fill_((raw_gu & 127) == 127, 0)
    raw_dn = torch.randint(0, 256, (e, H, I), device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8, generator=g)
    raw_dn.masked_fill_((raw_dn & 127) == 127, 0)
    gu = raw_gu.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    dn = raw_dn.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    gs = 0.0005 + torch.rand((e, 2 * I // 128, H // 128), device="cuda", generator=g) * 0.002
    ds = 0.0005 + torch.rand((e, H // 128, I // 128), device="cuda", generator=g) * 0.002
    return gu, gs, dn, ds

def stack_bytes(e=E):
    return e * 2 * I * H + e * H * I + (e * (2 * I // 128) * (H // 128) + e * (H // 128) * (I // 128)) * 4

def routing(t, seed):
    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
    x = torch.randn(t, H, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=g) * 0.1
    w, i = torch.rand(t, E, device="cuda", generator=g).topk(TOPK, dim=1)
    w = (w / w.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)).to(torch.bfloat16)
    return x, i.to(torch.int64), w

def out_hash(t):
    """Cross-run comparable bitwise hash of a bf16 tensor."""
    v = t.view(torch.int16).to(torch.int64)
    return f"sum={v.sum().item()} abs={v.abs().sum().item()} first={t.flatten()[0].item():.6e}"

import vkernels.torch_ops.glm_fp8_blockwise_gemm as G
HAS_INPLACE = hasattr(G, "e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace")

log(f"run label={LABEL} inplace_available={HAS_INPLACE}")
log(f"device: {torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)} hip={torch.version.hip}")
free, total = torch.cuda.mem_get_info()
log(f"memory: total={gib(total):.1f} GiB free={gib(free):.1f} GiB")
log(f"stack: E={E} H={H} I={I} bytes={stack_bytes()/2**30:.2f} GiB/layer")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- vk section
if "vk" in SECTIONS and HAS_INPLACE:
    log("== S2 single-layer: copy-convert vs in-place-convert ==")
    gu, gs, dn, ds = make_stack(11)
    x, idx, wts = routing(256, 21)

    torch.cuda.synchronize(); torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    base = torch.cuda.memory_allocated()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    gu_nz, gu_sc2 = G.e4m3fn_to_fnuz(gu, gs)
    dn_nz, dn_sc2 = G.e4m3fn_to_fnuz(dn, ds)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    t_old = time.perf_counter() - t0
    old_peak = gib(torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() - base)
    old_res = gib(torch.cuda.memory_allocated() - base)
    ref = G.glm_moe_grouped_gemm_native(x, gu_nz, gu_sc2, dn_nz, dn_sc2, idx, wts, swiglu_limit=SWIGLU)
    del gu_nz, gu_sc2, dn_nz, dn_sc2
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    log(f"OLD copy-convert : peak_transient+result={old_peak:.2f} GiB resident_after={old_res:.2f} GiB time={t_old*1e3:.0f} ms")

    ptr_gu, ptr_dn = gu.data_ptr(), dn.data_ptr()
    torch.cuda.synchronize(); torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    base = torch.cuda.memory_allocated()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    gu_nz2, gu_sc3 = G.e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(gu, gs, chunk_bytes=CHUNK)
    dn_nz2, dn_sc3 = G.e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(dn, ds, chunk_bytes=CHUNK)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    t_new = time.perf_counter() - t0
    new_peak = gib(torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() - base)
    new_res = gib(torch.cuda.memory_allocated() - base)
    log(f"NEW in-place     : peak_transient={new_peak:.2f} GiB resident_after={new_res:.2f} GiB time={t_new*1e3:.0f} ms")
    log(f"NEW storage identity: gu={gu_nz2.data_ptr()==ptr_gu} dn={dn_nz2.data_ptr()==ptr_dn} (must be True True)")
    got = G.glm_moe_grouped_gemm_native(x, gu_nz2, gu_sc3, dn_nz2, dn_sc3, idx, wts, swiglu_limit=SWIGLU)
    exact = torch.equal(got, ref)
    log(f"PARITY grouped old-vs-new stack: bit_exact={exact}")
    if not exact:
        log(f"  ref={out_hash(ref)}")
        log(f"  new={out_hash(got)}")

    log("== S2b fnuz-storage decode parity (convert in place, decode both ways) ==")
    sg, sgs, sd, sds = make_stack(31, e=8)
    xt, it, wt = routing(2, 41)
    ref_gu = G.expert_gemv(xt, sg, sgs, it)
    ref_dn = G.expert_gemv(ref_gu.chunk(2, -1)[0].sub(ref_gu.chunk(2, -1)[1]).clamp_(-7, 7).mul(0.288), sd, sds, it) if False else None
    sgu_nz, sgs2 = G.e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(sg, sgs, chunk_bytes=CHUNK)
    sdn_nz, sds2 = G.e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(sd, sds, chunk_bytes=CHUNK)
    got_gu = G.expert_gemv(xt, sgu_nz, sgs2, it, storage="e4m3fnuz")
    exact_gu = torch.equal(got_gu, ref_gu)
    log(f"PARITY expert_gemv fn vs fnuz-storage: bit_exact={exact_gu}")
    if not exact_gu:
        log(f"  ref={out_hash(ref_gu)}")
        log(f"  new={out_hash(got_gu)}")

# --------------------------------------------------------------- cap section
if "cap" in SECTIONS:
    log(f"== S3 K-layer sweep under the HBM floor (headroom target {HEADROOM_GIB:.0f} GiB) ==")
    stacks = []
    sb = stack_bytes()
    while True:
        free, _ = torch.cuda.mem_get_info()
        if gib(free) < HEADROOM_GIB + gib(sb):
            break
        stacks.append(make_stack(100 + len(stacks)))
    K = len(stacks)
    log(f"built K={K} layers x {gib(sb):.2f} GiB = {K*gib(sb):.1f} GiB resident; free now {gib(torch.cuda.mem_get_info()[0]):.1f} GiB")

    log("-- OLD path: copy-convert every layer (results kept, like the cache) --")
    converted, oom_at = 0, None
    kept = []
    torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    base = torch.cuda.memory_allocated()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        for i, (gu, gs, dn, ds) in enumerate(stacks):
            kept.append(G.e4m3fn_to_fnuz(gu, gs))
            kept.append(G.e4m3fn_to_fnuz(dn, ds))
            converted += 1
    except torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError:
        oom_at = converted
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    t_old = time.perf_counter() - t0
    old_peak = gib(torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() - base)
    if oom_at is not None:
        log(f"OLD: OOM at layer {oom_at}/{K} after converting {converted}/{K}; peak before OOM {old_peak:.1f} GiB, {t_old:.1f} s")
    else:
        log(f"OLD: converted {converted}/{K} (no OOM at this K); peak {old_peak:.1f} GiB, {t_old:.1f} s")
    del kept
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()

    if HAS_INPLACE:
        log("-- NEW path: in-place convert every layer (no results kept) --")
        torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
        base = torch.cuda.memory_allocated()
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        oom_new = None
        try:
            for i, (gu, gs, dn, ds) in enumerate(stacks):
                G.e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(gu, gs, chunk_bytes=CHUNK)
                G.e4m3fn_to_fnuz_inplace(dn, ds, chunk_bytes=CHUNK)
        except torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError:
            oom_new = i
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        t_new = time.perf_counter() - t0
        new_peak = gib(torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() - base)
        log(f"NEW: converted {('ALL %d' % K) if oom_new is None else str(oom_new)+'/'+str(K)}; peak {new_peak:.2f} GiB, {t_new:.1f} s, resident_delta={gib(torch.cuda.memory_allocated()-base):.3f} GiB")

        log("-- grouped forward on every converted layer (all-layers grouping) --")
        x, idx, wts = routing(256, 21)
        hashes, grouped_ok = [], 0
        torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
        base = torch.cuda.memory_allocated()
        try:
            for i, (gu, gs, dn, ds) in enumerate(stacks):
                out = G.glm_moe_grouped_gemm_native(
                    x, gu.view(torch.float8_e4m3fnuz), gs, dn.view(torch.float8_e4m3fnuz), ds,
                    idx, wts, swiglu_limit=SWIGLU)
                hashes.append(out_hash(out))
                grouped_ok += 1
                del out
        except torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError:
            log(f"NEW: grouped OOM at layer {grouped_ok}")
        log(f"NEW: grouped forward OK on {grouped_ok}/{K} layers; peak {gib(torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()-base):.2f} GiB")
        log(f"NEW_HASH_S3 layer0: {hashes[0] if hashes else 'NONE'}")

# -------------------------------------------------------------- floe section
if "floe" in SECTIONS:
    log("== S5 floe Glm53Experts level ==")
    os.environ["GLM53_FP8_GROUPED"] = "1"
    os.environ["GLM53_BATCHED_EXPERTS"] = "0"
    os.environ["GLM53_FUSED_GEMV"] = "1"
    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, os.environ.get("PROF71_FLOE_REPO", "/iopsstor/scratch/cscs/xyao/floe-beverin/glm5-smoke/repo"))
    from floe.engine.runner.models.glm5.arch import Glm53Experts
    from floe.engine.runner.models.glm5.config import Glm53Config
    import floe
    log(f"floe from: {floe.__file__}")

    cfg = Glm53Config(n_routed_experts=E, hidden_size=H, moe_intermediate_size=I)
    KF = 3
    layers = []
    base_alloc = torch.cuda.memory_allocated()
    for li in range(KF):
        with torch.device("meta"):
            m = Glm53Experts(cfg)
        gu, gs, dn, ds = make_stack(200 + li)
        m.gate_up_proj = torch.nn.Parameter(gu, requires_grad=False)
        m.gate_up_scale = gs
        m.down_proj = torch.nn.Parameter(dn, requires_grad=False)
        m.down_scale = ds
        layers.append(m)
    stacks_gib = KF * gib(stack_bytes())
    log(f"built {KF} floe layers, fp8 stacks resident={gib(torch.cuda.memory_allocated()-base_alloc):.2f} GiB")

    x, idx, wts = routing(256, 21)
    torch.cuda.synchronize(); torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    base = torch.cuda.memory_allocated()
    outs = []
    ptrs_before = [m.gate_up_proj.data_ptr() for m in layers]
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    for m in layers:
        outs.append(m(x, idx, wts))
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    t_grouped = time.perf_counter() - t0
    delta = gib(torch.cuda.memory_allocated() - base)
    peak = gib(torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() - base)
    which = "inplace-marker" if hasattr(layers[0], "_fp8_inplace_key") else ("copy-cache" if hasattr(layers[0], "_fp8_grouped_cache") else "grouped-NOT-engaged")
    log(f"grouped T=256 x{KF} layers: impl={which} resident_delta={delta:.2f} GiB peak={peak:.2f} GiB time={t_grouped*1e3:.0f} ms")
    if hasattr(layers[0], "_fp8_inplace_key"):
        same_ptr = all(m.gate_up_proj.data_ptr() == p for m, p in zip(layers, ptrs_before))
        log(f"in-place identity: gate_up data_ptr unchanged={same_ptr} (must be True)")
    log(f"HASH_T256: {out_hash(outs[0])}")

    del outs
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    # decode after conversion (T=2 <= decode cap): exercises the storage-aware
    # decode paths on converted (new) / untouched (old) buffers
    x2, idx2, w2 = routing(2, 22)
    outs2 = []
    for m in layers:
        outs2.append(m(x2, idx2, w2))
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    log(f"HASH_T2: {out_hash(outs2[0])}")
    del outs2

    # grouped again post-decode: marker must hold, no reconversion
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    out = layers[0](x, idx, wts)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    log(f"re-grouped after decode: time={(time.perf_counter()-t0)*1e3:.0f} ms (no reconversion => fast)")
    log(f"HASH_T256_AGAIN: {out_hash(out)}")

log("PROF71_DONE")

content.text: continue

Mystery solved — it's **my harness bug**, not a kernel/platform issue: `routing()` always does topk over E=288, but S2b's stack has only **8 experts** → the gemv reads expert IDs up to 287 → out-of-bounds (the kernel intentionally doesn't bounds-check indices, as documented). That explains every fault *and* why RUN 2's floe decode (E=288 stack, in-bounds) sailed through, plus the `nan` in my first repro. The pytest batch failures were separately caused by corrupt triton-cache entries left by the aborted RUN 1.

Fixing the harness and the uncommitted test fix:

def routing(t, seed, e=E):
    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
    x = torch.randn(t, H, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=g) * 0.1
    w, i = torch.rand(t, e, device="cuda", generator=g).topk(TOPK, dim=1)
    w = (w / w.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)).to(torch.bfloat16)
    return x, i.to(torch.int64), w
